title: Optimized Nonlinear Grey Bernoulli Model for Nowcasting the Philippine Gross Domestic Product
authors: Carillo, Shan Kierstin; Serra, Ian Jay
venue: European Journal of Pure and Applied Mathematics
tldr: PSO-optimized NGBM(1,1) achieves 5.45% MAPE in nowcasting Philippine quarterly GDP, outperforming standard grey models.
problem_and_motivation: Accurate and timely GDP estimates are essential for economic policymaking, but official statistics are released with considerable delay of up to two months. Nowcasting—predicting the present or very near future using available data—is critical for evidence-based governance. Standard grey models like NGBM(1,1) perform well with small samples but their accuracy depends heavily on precise parameter estimation, particularly the power index and background value coefficient. Philippine quarterly GDP data exhibits strong seasonal patterns (Q1 decline, Q4 surge) that standard grey models fail to capture, necessitating optimized approaches.
approach: Nonlinear Grey Bernoulli Model NGBM(1,1) extended with Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to optimize power index m and background value coefficient α simultaneously.
Exponential background value refinement from Cheng et al. reformulates the background value using an exponential curve for enhanced responsiveness to dynamic patterns.
Harmonic function simulation study evaluates 70/30 vs 80/20 training-to-testing splits across 15 parameter combinations of cyclical amplitudes.
Quarterly Philippine GDP data from Q1 2021 to Q4 2024 (constant 2018 USD) sourced from Philippine Statistics Authority OpenSTAT portal.
Out-of-sample evaluation using MAPE and RMSE, with seasonal decomposition to address systematic Q4 prediction errors.
findings: num: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieves the lowest out-of-sample MAPE of 5.45% and RMSE of 362,077.8 million PHP.
num: Seasonal adjustment dramatically improves all models to below 1% MAPE, with PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieving 0.38%.
num: PSO algorithm converges within approximately 30 iterations, demonstrating efficient parameter optimization.
num: PSO-NGBM(1,1) outperforms in 12 of 15 simulation parameter combinations under the 70/30 split.
num: Near-perfect prediction in 2024 Q2 with prediction error of 0.0001% after seasonal adjustment.
num: Exponential background value method yields minimal additional gains over standard NGBM(1,1) beyond PSO optimization.
num: All models show consistent Q4 prediction errors ranging from 7.73% to 10.48% before seasonal adjustment.

definitions.definition: Extension of GM(1,1) incorporating Bernoulli differential equation for nonlinear systems modeling with small samples.
Prediction of the present, very near future, or very recent past using currently available data.
Particle Swarm Optimization, metaheuristic algorithm inspired by collective behavior of bird flocks for parameter optimization.
Cumulative summation transformation applied to raw data to smooth series for grey model processing.
Weighted average of consecutive accumulated values that forms the basis for parameter estimation in grey models.
Alternative background value formulation using exponential curve between consecutive time points for improved dynamic responsiveness.

topics.name: Existing Personal Finance Systems Landscape
topics.justification: While primarily macroeconomic, GDP nowcasting provides foundational economic indicators that personal finance systems rely upon for contextual financial planning and spending behavior modeling.

topics.name: Predictive Modeling in Personal Finance Systems
topics.justification: The PSO-optimized NGBM(1,1) demonstrates predictive modeling techniques applicable to financial time series, though applied at macro level rather than individual financial behavior.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This study demonstrates that metaheuristic optimization (PSO) substantially improves grey model forecasting for Philippine GDP nowcasting. The key innovation is combining PSO with NGBM(1,1) to simultaneously optimize the power index and background value coefficient, achieving 5.45% out-of-sample MAPE. The dramatic improvement after seasonal adjustment (below 1% MAPE) highlights the critical role of accounting for seasonal patterns in economic time series. The 70/30 training-to-testing ratio is validated through simulation as optimal for limited quarterly data.
directly_justifies: PSO-NGBM(1,1) achieves 5.45% out-of-sample MAPE, the lowest among all compared grey models.
Seasonal adjustment reduces MAPE from over 5% to below 1% across all models.
PSO algorithm converges efficiently within approximately 30 iterations.
70/30 data split validated as optimal through simulation across 15 parameter combinations.
Near-perfect prediction (0.0001% error) achieved in 2024 Q2 after seasonal adjustment.
limits: Grey models require strictly non-negative input data and fixed frequency, limiting applicability to diverse financial datasets.
The model cannot capture sharp quarterly fluctuations and seasonal dynamics without separate preprocessing.
Small dataset of only 16 quarterly observations constrains model complexity and validation robustness.
No comparison with modern machine learning approaches (LSTM, ARIMA, neural networks) for comprehensive benchmarking.
Exponential background value method provides minimal improvement over standard NGBM(1,1), questioning its additional complexity.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. Medium relevance was assigned to existing personal finance systems landscape (4.B) because GDP nowcasting provides economic context relevant to personal financial planning systems, and to predictive modeling (6.A) because the optimization techniques demonstrated are applicable to financial time series forecasting. High relevance topics rejected as the paper focuses on macroeconomic forecasting rather than personal financial behavior, spending analysis, or individual financial systems. The paper's contribution to personal finance is indirect, providing economic indicators rather than personal financial tools or behavioral insights.
